day.note: I'm Meowfia, so I want a Farm player eggsecuted. I'll stay quiet to avoid defending Finley openly, and at eggsecution throw at Blair, who is pushing the vote.

Alex.note: I'm Farm with a Tit. Drew claimed Turkey last round, so I'll visit Drew and guess Turkey, which gains an egg if right.

Blair.note: I'm Farm with the Falcon again. Drew has been consistent and quiet, so I'll visit Drew to learn who they visited.

Casey.note: I'm Farm with a Hawk, and Ellis is far ahead, so I need to find Meowfia. Alex's shifting claims and early push on Blair make Alex my best Hawk visit.

Drew.note: As Meowfia Sphinx, I learn the farm roles are Falcon, Hawk, Tit, Turkey. I'll pick Turkey, a stay-home role, to identify that player.

Finley.note: I'm Meowfia as the Mouser this round. Ellis leads on points, so I'll visit Ellis to learn their role.

Ellis lays 1 egg in Finley's nest

Alex.feeling: Messy round: Ellis's collapse and Finley's Mouser claim look suspicious, but Casey and Blair's role claims are also hard to verify, so I'm not fully certain.

Blair.feeling: Round 3 is tense: Ellis's collapse right after Finley's Mouser claim makes Finley the prime suspect, but Casey's Hawk check and Alex's Tit guess are hard to verify, so I'm working from thin evidence.

Casey.feeling: Tense and muddled: Finley's Mouser claim right after Ellis's collapse looks suspicious, but Drew and Blair both have unverifiable stories, so I'm not fully certain.

Drew.feeling: As the Meowfia Sphinx I know the Farm roles, so the day is tense but I'm confident Finley, who claimed Mouser, is my teammate and the table is pinning the wrong people.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and confusing: I'm already dead, and the table is split between Finley's Mouser claim and Casey's Hawk claim, with few checks that hold up.

Finley.feeling: Tense: I'm Meowfia, Ellis collapsed right after my Mouser claim, and Blair and Casey have both called to vote me, so I'm likely to be eggsecuted.

Alex.note: Finley's Mouser claim and Ellis's collapse point to Finley as Meowfia. I'll throw three cards at Finley to make sure the vote lands.

Blair.note: I'm throwing at Finley, the suspected Mouser, with two low cards and keeping my higher cards as a floor.

Casey.note: Finley is my suspected Meowfia after the Mouser claim and Ellis's collapse, and Blair and Alex are backing the same vote. I'll throw two mid cards at Finley to make sure the vote lands and keep my high cards.

Drew.note: Throw at Blair, a Farm player, so if we lose my single highest thrown card returns. I'll throw two low cards to draw votes away from Finley.

Ellis.note: I'm dead. Finley's Mouser claim and visit to me look like Meowfia, so I'll throw my two highest cards at Finley to bank value if Farm wins.

Finley.note: I'm Meowfia, so I want a Farm player eggsecuted. Blair is leading the vote against me, so I'll throw at Blair with two low cards.

Alex.confusing: The Eggsecution scoring was hard to track: a losing side's throws get discarded, but a throw at the other team returns your highest card, so the real cost of each throw was unclear. The interplay of visit reports and Turkey/Eagle egg counts also made it easy to misread who had really visited whom.
Alex.fun: Round 3's day, when Finley's Mouser claim and Ellis's collapse lined up and the table turned on Finley, was the most tense moment. Watching the votes stack up and the Meowfia get caught was satisfying.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since confused reports and mismatched egg counts made the day discussion hard to pin down.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I threw at Finley and backed the vote against Casey, but I was Meowfia and should have sided with Casey as a teammate instead of voting against them. I would have kept my cards and avoided pushing the table toward a wrong target.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey rule tripped me up: I first thought the Turkey gains the egg, when the visitor gains it. My confused Kookaburra report also left me unable to vouch for my own visit.
Blair.fun: Round 1 went well: I flagged Casey's Mouser claim right after Ellis collapsed, and the table eggsecuted Casey as Meowfia.
Blair.change: I'd make it clearer when a Wink is used and who holds one, since silent collapses were hard to read.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I threw at Alex, a Farm Falcon, on shifting-role suspicion, and I got eggsecuted. I should have thrown at Casey, the Floofer Meowfia, whom I hadn't yet ruled out.

Casey.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track, since Blair's confused report made their visit claims unreliable for the whole table. Turkey egg timing was also easy to misread at first.
Casey.fun: Round 1 was a tense shootout: my Mouser claim on the Tit was real, but Ellis's collapse made the whole table suspect me.
Casey.change: I'd make the role reveals and egg changes clearer for everyone, so a Turkey's egg and a Hawk's result are easier to check without re-reading the rules.
Casey.regret: I winked Ellis, a real Farm Tit, right after my Mouser claim, which made the table suspect me. I'd hold the Wink until the vote, or use it only when it cannot point straight back at me.

Drew.confusing: The Turkey egg timing was hard to track: a Turkey gains the visitor an egg, which I first misread as the Turkey gaining. Round 3 also had a Turkey who reported nobody visited while a visitor's egg showed otherwise.
Drew.fun: Round 3 as the Sphinx, finding the Turkey and then watching the table argue over Finley's Mouser claim while I stayed quiet. Also Ellis's collapse right after Casey's Mouser claim in round 1.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about which egg came from which visit, so players don't have to reason through Turkey and Eagle counts to check claims.
Drew.regret: In round 3, I threw two cards at Blair instead of backing a clear read, and I wrongly thought Casey was Meowfia in round 1 based on thin evidence. Next time I'd hold my throws until a claim is actually contradicted.

Ellis.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to misread: I first thought the Turkey gained eggs from visitors, when the visitor is the one who gains. That confusion made the dawn reports harder to check.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Casey's Mouser visit to me and the Falcon report lined up, and the table voted Casey out. Banking my two highest cards on the win felt good.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports spell out who gained or lost eggs and why, so players can check visit claims without mixing up roles.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I pressed Drew's Turkey claim using the wrong egg rule, which was a bad read. Knowing the truth, I'd check the visit rule before accusing anyone.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle count rule and the Turkey egg were easy to mix up at the table: a Turkey's egg goes to its visitor, so I briefly misreported my own gain as zero in round 3. The dead-player throw rule was also unclear to me.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was fun: my Eagle count of zero for Alex clashed with Drew's claimed visit, and the table spent the whole day arguing over who was lying.
Finley.change: Make the dawn report say which role gave each egg, so players can check Turkey and Eagle claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I should have kept my Mouser claim quiet and voted with the table instead of drawing fire by claiming a role that had just been tied to a winked Turkey. Knowing Ellis was the Turkey and Drew the Sphinx, I would have pressed Drew harder.

review.title: The Ellis Runaway
review.headline: Ellis banked 52 points by throwing high cards at winning votes, three rounds running.
review.summary: Farm won rounds 1 and 3 by voting out a Meowfia who had just winked someone. Round 2 went to Meowfia when the table eggsecuted a confused Kookaburra. Ellis, the Tit in round 1 and a Sphinx and then a Turkey after that, won all three rounds and threw big cards each time. He finished with 52 points, more than double second place. The other five players were playing for second from round 2 on.

rounds.recap: Casey (Mouser) winked Ellis (Tit) mid-day, which pointed straight at Casey, since only Casey had claimed a cat role that visited Ellis. Farm voted Casey out. Ellis was dead but still threw 19 points of cards and won big.

Casey (Floofer) hugged Blair, which confused her. Blair's confusion plus her shifting claims made her the easy vote. Ellis, a Meowfia Sphinx, learned Alex was Farm and threw at Alex. Farm still eggsecuted Blair, so Meowfia won and Ellis banked 15.

Finley (Mouser) winked Ellis, the Turkey, and then claimed Mouser openly, which made him the obvious suspect. Four players threw at him and he was eggsecuted. Ellis was dead but won again and banked 15, finishing on 52.

highlights.text: Casey winked Ellis the moment Ellis accused him. This proved Casey was the Mouser and sank him.
Blair opened by announcing she was confused. The table then voted for her anyway, and that was the wrong vote.
Finley winked Ellis and then claimed the Mouser role himself. Blair, Casey and Alex all pointed at him, and he was voted out.
Drew's Sphinx told him Ellis was the Turkey. He defended Finley but threw at Blair, so his teammate was eggsecuted regardless.

confusions.what: Said his Kookaburra report gave no role for Alex. He was hugged, so his action did nothing. He seemed not to understand that.
Claimed to be Floofer and Farm side. The Floofer is always a cat, so this was a bad claim.
Misread the Turkey rule and said Drew's nest should have gained an egg. She retracted this in beat 3.
Also had the Turkey rule backwards, then corrected it.
Said Casey was 'out this round'. Casey was alive and had visited her.
Said he gained no eggs, though he had drawn one from the Turkey. He had to correct himself.
Doubted Blair for switching from Falcon to Kookaburra. Roles are re-dealt every round, so that proves nothing. The whole table made this mistake.
Said Finley's claim to have visited a Turkey was suspect because he gained no egg. This was wrong, because the Turkey gives its visitors an egg.

worked: The Mouser's Wink gives Meowfia a real tempo play. In round 1 it created a clear accusation, and in round 3 the Wink killed the leader.
The Turkey rule gave a checkable puzzle. The extra eggs in the nests of Drew and Finley both pointed back to Ellis, and Blair's Falcon result confirmed it.
Hug and confusion in round 2 gave a believable false trail. Blair's confused report made her the scapegoat for a Meowfia win.
problems: Ellis ran away with the game. He won all three rounds and threw 19, 15 and 15 points of cards while dead or alive. With 37 points after round 2, nobody could catch him. Consider a cap on points per round, or a catch-up rule for the leader, because the final round had no stakes.
The 'only first place wins' rule did not shape play. Nobody tried to stop Ellis or throw at him. His teammates and opponents all helped him bank points. Players needed some way to hurt the leader.

Winking the loudest accuser hands Meowfia's identity to the table. It happened twice, and both Wink users were voted out the same day. Make the Wink harder to trace, or make it less obvious who had the means.
The dead can still throw their highest cards and bank them with no risk. Ellis banked 19 points in round 1 after he was dead. A dead player should throw fewer cards, or at lower value.

Meowfia did not know each other, but this rarely mattered. Round 2 was the only real test, and it was lost for lack of a visible reason to vote Blair. Hawk and Eagle also made little difference. Many night actions gave results nobody could use, which left the talk repetitive.
